perspective: Adversarial verification of batch operations, reminders, scheduling, and deadline semantics across Mayra, Laura, Daisy, and derived pipeline artifacts.

findings.claim: Faculty outreach is currently a bulk/manual email operation, with per-recipient responses and follow-up; no confirmed automated scheduler exists.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:12-20, 32-35 (Mayra sends collective email and receives replies)
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:248-256 (Mayra chases non-responses)
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:111-124 (Ian proposes date-triggered bulk renewal emails; Mayra accepts conceptually)
HR App (1).docx:1102-1117 (faculty form is future state; current process remains email-based)
findings.risk: Treating a proposed scheduler or form as current policy could send unauthorized or mistimed messages and obscure unanswered faculty requests.
findings.recommendation: Model bulk outreach, reminder cadence, audience, sender, and activation as explicit configuration requiring approval; preserve current email workflow as the evidenced baseline.

findings.claim: Reminder cadence is not established as a policy. Mayra requests tracking/reminders, but no interval, maximum, escalation, or stop condition is confirmed.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:248-256 (requests chasing or a reminder for outstanding confirmations; no cadence)
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:127-131 (describes chasing as current work)
HR App (1).docx:1110-1117 (faculty non-response requires chasing; no closure rule)
HR App (1).docx:281-297 (Laura uses escalating templates, but no fixed schedule is stated)
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:55-59 (Ian says 'repeat every three days'; this is Ian's proposed automation, not Daisy's reported policy)
findings.risk: A three-day repeat could be incorrectly treated as approved business policy; indefinite reminders could create spam, duplicate outreach, or no auditable closure.
findings.recommendation: Record cadence, maximum attempts, escalation/owner, quiet periods, and terminal outcomes as unresolved policy decisions. Label 'every three days' proposed only.

findings.claim: Laura sends hiring-authority DocuSign requests in batches of approximately 20, not all at once; this is current practice, not a system guarantee.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:244-260 (Laura sends about 20 to the hiring authority at a time; returned as one DocuSign; then sends to students)
HR App (1).docx:217-230 (sent/signed statuses are manually tracked and signed documents downloaded)
student_hiring_pipeline.md:24-26 (derived artifact records about-20 batching and signed-and-screening-cleared gate)
findings.risk: The transcript does not define batch selection rules, partial failure handling, duplicate prevention, batch-level versus individual status, or whether the batch size is a hard limit.
findings.recommendation: Represent approximately 20 as an observed operating habit. Do not encode it as a hard policy without owner confirmation; retain per-document status and audit identity.

findings.claim: Foreign-principal screening is currently initiated manually per student, with bulk volume observed around 50 students; bulk screening automation is proposed/attempted, not proven.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:611-637 (Laura manually enters each student into the screening website; prior automation attempt was disrupted by a form change)
HR App (1).docx:669-682 (Laura says bulk periods can involve 50 students and manual submissions take time)
HR App (1).docx:78-87 (screening is a gate before offer issuance; Laura chases non-completers)
student_hiring_pipeline.md:62 (derived artifact summarizes manual web form per student and about 50 at a time)
findings.risk: A bulk-screening feature could be mistaken for an available integration even though the external form changed and no successful integration is evidenced.
findings.recommendation: Treat screening submission as an external manual step unless a tested integration and ownership are separately proven. Keep one status/audit record per student.

findings.claim: Payroll proximity drives ad hoc chasing, but no exact deadline semantics are established for student signatures or screening.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:251-260 (Laura chases unsigned students because payroll is approaching)
HR App (1).docx:281-297 (Laura uses scenario-specific escalation templates, including pay/access consequences and start-date changes)
HR App (1).docx:120-130 (Oracle approval can sit for weeks depending on effective date; Laura rechecks)
student_hiring_pipeline.md:29 (derived artifact correctly notes approval queue may take weeks, but does not establish a deadline policy)
findings.risk: 'Payroll approaching' is a trigger/context, not a defined SLA or cutoff. Automated reminders could promise or enforce deadlines not authorized by HR.
findings.recommendation: Track effective date, payroll-impact date, last action, and owner separately. Leave cutoff, escalation, and start-date-change rules open.

findings.claim: Finance uses pay periods and check dates to time costing, and costing must occur by a pay-period deadline; exact dates and deadline owner are not present in the interview evidence.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:454-472 (Daisy consults an annually updated pay-period/check-date calendar and says costing must be changed in Oracle by the relevant time)
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:88-101 (distribution is calculated within the applicable biweekly pay period)
daisy_finance_stage.md:23-28 (derived artifact states per-pay-period 100% distribution and Oracle entry by deadline)
daisy_finance_stage.md:101-106 (exact Oracle deadline and entering owner remain open questions)
findings.risk: A scheduler cannot safely infer due dates from check dates alone; pay-period boundaries, effective dates, lead time, holidays, corrections, and timezone/ownership are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Use the authoritative annual payroll calendar as data, version it by year, and require explicit deadline calculation/ownership before automation.

findings.claim: The only explicit semester timing is approximate planning context, not a binding deadline: Mayra usually asks faculty around February for May-start work and Laura begins around March.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:924-927 (Laura says Mayra usually asks around February; work reaches Laura around March for May start)
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:421-441 (Mayra says graduate students usually have a deadline; no date or rule is supplied)
HR App (1).docx:914-918 (September is discussed as a project timeline, not an operational processing deadline)
findings.risk: Turning approximate interview timing into hard scheduled outreach could create false deadline compliance and miss exceptions such as mid-semester OPS appointments.
findings.recommendation: Store semester timing as planning guidance only. Require a term-specific, owner-approved deadline and exception path before scheduled bulk sends.

findings.claim: The derived artifacts overstate automation/currentness by presenting a mid-semester form-link path and reminder loops as confirmed, while primary interviews describe them as proposed or unspecified.
evidence: mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:48-49, 67, 114 (marks mid-semester form link as confirmed/current)
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:427-441 (Mayra asks whether a form could exist; Ian proposes adding a form-link step)
HR App (1).docx:1102-1117 (Laura says faculty form is future state and current practice remains email-based)
daisy_finance_stage.md:18-32 and 101-106 (derived loops/deadlines include unresolved semantics)
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:55-59 (three-day repeat is proposed by Ian)
findings.risk: Downstream design or implementation could encode proposed automation as approved policy and silently change who is contacted, when, and under what deadline.
findings.recommendation: Reclassify form-link, three-day reminders, bulk scheduler, and exact deadline behavior as proposed/unresolved unless a later owner decision or live implementation proves them.

missing_or_ambiguous: Approved reminder cadence, maximum attempts, escalation path, quiet hours, and closure status.
Whether reminders are sent by Mayra, Laura, a generic mailbox, or another approved sender.
Selection rules and idempotency for faculty, screening, and DocuSign batches; whether approximately 20 is a soft practice or hard limit.
Bulk-screening integration ownership and behavior after the external form changes.
Exact semester deadlines for faculty submissions, new hires, mid-semester OPS appointments, and change requests.
Authoritative payroll calendar source, annual versioning, lead time, timezone, and exact Oracle costing deadline.
Meaning of Daisy's post-entry row status (transcribed as 'page', probably 'paid') and its deadline semantics.
Handling of partial batch success, duplicate sends, bounced messages, withdrawn appointments, and late responses.
Whether automated scheduling is approved policy or only Ian's proposed future-state automation.
